problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
{t}^{2}{y}^{″}+13t{y}^{′}+36y=0,\,t>0.
$$
worked_solution:
The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={t}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $t$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {t}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda -2}+13t\cdot \lambda {t}^{\lambda -1}+36{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){t}^{\lambda }+13\lambda {t}^{\lambda }+36{t}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {t}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)+13\lambda +36] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)+13\lambda +36 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+12\lambda +36 & =0 \\ (\lambda +6)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have a double root $\lambda =-6.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(t)={c}_{1}{t}^{-6}+{c}_{2}{t}^{-6}\operatorname{ln}⁡t.
$$
